fields.description:
## Problem

`/mcp` can return persistent HTTP 502 after concurrent gate load if nginx's single-server upstream points at a dead MCP container. Parent `witted-invisible-roan` made autodeploy retain a crashed live backend instead of deleting it, but recovery can still wait for Docker/humans.

## RCA / design decision

Related load-side ticket `enduring-ironclad-arrowana` already removed the biggest measured retained-memory multiplier: retained plan-review snapshot state fell from 256,646,460 bytes to 37,046 bytes on a 9,081-ticket store. This ticket fixes the serving-path residue.

Selected prevention: an autodeploy in-place watchdog for the live MCP backend. On each serialized autodeploy tick (the existing flock owns check/start/readiness/backoff), `MCP_SELF_HEAL` defaults to `1` inside `autodeploy.sh` so the fix is active after merge; setting it to `0` is the kill switch. The watchdog uses the existing `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` readiness deadline. If `MCP_SELF_HEAL=1` and the nginx upstream port maps to a managed MCP container that is not running, autodeploy runs `docker start <live-container>` and readiness-checks that same port. A healthy running backend is a strict no-op. The port-to-container lookup must work for exited containers using inspect data, not `docker port` alone. Success leaves nginx byte-identical, clears MCP backoff, and logs recovery; failure leaves the container/upstream identity intact, emits existing `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR mcp-live-backend-down`, records MCP backoff, and remains a retryable transient path; repeated backoff cycles are the operator escalation signal for a fatal start/config problem. `MCP_SELF_HEAL=0` disables the new branch and restores log-and-wait behavior.

Rejected alternatives: blue/green self-heal doubles MCP memory under pressure; nginx passive failover needs an already-live spare; Docker `--restart always` is already present but is passive and not readiness/log evidenced; healthcheck watchdog/autoheal prior art supports this design and is implemented here through the existing autodeploy tick instead of a new daemon; instance sizing/off-box gates remain with `inherited-americium-porpoise`.

## Testing / verification plan

- RED test in `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`: no source change pending, nginx points at an exited managed MCP backend, one tick runs `docker start` for that exact container, upstream remains unchanged, success log appears, and readiness passes.
- RED test for failure/kill switch: failed start or readiness does not remove the dead live backend, upstream remains unchanged, `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR ... mcp-live-backend-down` appears, MCP backoff is recorded, and `MCP_SELF_HEAL=0` skips restart.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` and full `make verify` before push.
- Live check after merge: inspect `/mcp/health` and autodeploy logs; no Terraform apply is required because failure visibility reuses existing deploy_errors wiring and success is operator-visible journald evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The selected design is recorded with why alternatives were accepted/rejected.
- [ ] A simulated MCP backend death recovers without persistent nginx 502.
- [ ] The prevention is covered by tests and visible through existing deploy-error alarm wiring plus logs.
- [ ] Capacity/concurrency measurements cite `enduring-ironclad-arrowana` and the residual campaign `inherited-americium-porpoise`.
